subject: SpinLoop hosted API — post-call: usage profile & pricing slab options
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Velasquez <sofia@spinloop.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: SpinLoop hosted API — post-call: usage profile & pricing slab options

Hi Sofia — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and the asks we left with: 

Call recap
- Product: SpinLoop intends to power in-chat AI suggestions in the mobile app for release v1 (MVP).
- Expected behavior: synchronous generation for short responses (~40–150 tokens per response, median ~70), occasional longer snippets (~400 tokens) for explanation flows.
- Integration mode: hosted API (no private deployment initially).

Quantities we discussed (please confirm):
- Expected monthly tokens (aggregate): ~300–400M tokens/month (ballpark).
- Expected steady-state TPS (peak busy minute): 30–60 TPS (45 TPS was called out as typical peak during promo spikes).
- Target price range: $8k–$12k/month initially (procurement budget band).

Next steps / asks for you
1) Confirm an expected monthly token range (low / best / high). If you can share a short CSV of anticipated daily request counts, attach and we’ll run a modeled cost run.
2) Confirm realistic peak TPS for a worst-case 5–10 minute window.
3) Any procurement constraints on minimum contract term or prepayment for committed pricing?

Attached: SpinLoop_MVP_traffic_snapshot.csv — the export you shared on the call (I kept the example rows and normalized traffic).

Pricing note (high-level): we discussed three approaches — pay-as-you-go (self-serve), committed slab (1/3/12 month commitments), and reserved capacity (dedicated burst pools). I’ll prepare simple $/1M-token scenarios and a straw-man slab that maps into your $8–12k target once you confirm the numbers above.

Thanks — happy to jump on 30m next week for quick walk-through of the cost scenarios.

— Priyom
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Sofia Velasquez <sofia@spinloop.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SpinLoop hosted API — post-call: usage profile & pricing slab options

Hi Priyom — thanks for the summary, that looks right. Quick answers below: 

1) Monthly tokens: low ~250M, best ~350M, high ~500M (the product analytics team ran some conservative forecasts; I attached the small CSV we used during the call).
2) Peak TPS: realistic peak 45 TPS; extreme promotional peak up to ~65 TPS for ~10 minutes but we expect those spikes to be rare.
3) Procurement: we prefer 6–12 month commitments if the unit economics are attractive; for pilots we can do month-to-month but with a fixed $/1M target.

Budget: the $8k–$12k/month is the operating budget band they gave me. If committed pricing with a 6–12 month term can hit $/1M tokens in the ballpark of $20–$35 per 1M tokens (depending on token-count assumptions), procurement will push internally. If pricing is higher, we’ll need to show clear latency and SLO advantages vs open-source self-hosting.

Happy to have a short call Tue 10–10:30 PT next week.

— Sofia
Head of Product Operations, SpinLoop
sofia@spinloop.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: SpinLoop hosted API — post-call: usage profile & pricing slab options

Priyom / Karthik — looping you both in with a quick pricing sketch based on Sofia’s numbers. I ran three scenario buckets and included unit $/1M calculations; attaching the sheet (pricing_options_calc.xlsx).

Assumptions used (from Sofia): median response 70 tokens, avg tokens per request = 90 (accounts for context + response), sessions/day scaled to monthly tokens given their low/best/high.

Scenario A: Self-serve / Pay-as-you-go
- Price: $40 per 1M tokens (published hosted list; no commitment)
- Cost @ 350M tokens: 350 * $40 = $14,000/month
- Peak handling: fine for bursts; no SLA credit or reserved pools

Scenario B: Committed slab (6 month) — recommended for MVP
- Proposed slab: 300M tokens/month committed at $28 per 1M
- Overage: $45 per 1M
- Effective cost @ 350M tokens (50M overage): (300*$28)+(50*$45)= $8,400 + $2,250 = $10,650/month
- $/1M effective = $30.43

Scenario C: Reserved burst-enabled (dedicated capacity)
- Fixed monthly reserved fee + per-token: reserved fee $5,000 + $18 per 1M tokens for usage up to 600M
- Effective cost @ 350M: $5,000 + (350*$18) = $5,000 + $6,300 = $11,300/month
- $/1M effective = $32.29

Notes and commentary:
- If SpinLoop commits to 12 months at the slab in B, we can push the slab price to $24 per 1M and reduce effective $/1M to ~ $27–28 at 350M tokens. That would align with their $8k–12k budget band depending on exact volume.
- Peak TPS 45 is within typical hosted capacity; if they require strict latency SLOs during their promo spikes we should propose a short-term burst pool and standard fallback policy (route to compatible cheaper variant if reserved capacity is saturated).
- Attachments: the calc sheet shows the breakpoints and a short sensitivity table for 250/350/500M cases.

Action items I recommend now:
1) Priyom — send Sofia a 1-page strawman with the 3 scenarios and the 6-month vs 12-month committed rate (show example effective $/1M for low/best/high).
2) Karthik — can you confirm whether we can offer a temporary promotional slab for first 3 months (to help SpinLoop hit their UX goals) and what guardrails (min commit, up-front payment) we’d require?
3) Priyom — schedule Tue 10–10:30 PT call and include a one-slide latency/SLO comparison for the reserved vs slab options.

I think Scenario B (6 month committed slab) is the best tradeoff to put in front of procurement given their budget.

— Marissa
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: pricing_options_calc.xlsx (contains scenario math and sensitivity), notes in-sheet.

Thanks Marissa — I’ll put the 1-page strawman together and share before EOD. For the Tue slot I confirmed with Sofia; I’ll send a calendar invite to include a short live calculator walk-through.

Quick note for the quote: if procurement asks for an explicit $/1M target range, we should lead with the 6-month committed slab at $28/1M as the headline (effective ~$30/1M at 350M with modest overage), and offer a 12-month incentive (drop to $24/1M headline). I’ll flag the up-front payment/commitment terms in the sheet.

Karthik — are you OK to own the promo slab guardrails? If yes I’ll include the mechanics in the strawman.

— Priyom
